notes: Ladder network: three horizontal rails (top y~136-145, middle y~255-262, bottom y~382-392) tied together by five vertical columns at x~50, 182, 262, 370, 456. Each rail is BROKEN by a series element, which is what creates most of the nets. Coords are 512-space. 0 = the middle rail from GND 15 (drawn rotated 90 deg at the far left, x~10) rightwards to the LEFT plate of capacitor 9 at x~221: GND 15, V-AC 0 bottom, I-DC 3 top (junction blob at (49,256)), zener 4 bottom and diode 16 top (drawn junction CIRCLE at (182,255)), capacitor 9 left plate. 0 also covers the SECOND, physically separate ground node at the bottom right: resistor 13 bottom lead -> down x~473 -> GND 7 at (470,388). Per the protocol all GND symbols are one reference, so both nodes are named '0'. Note GND 7's lead does NOT touch the bottom rail - the bottom rail's right end corners at (445,385) and runs left, ~7 px clear of the GND 7 bar stack (checked at 14x). n1 = top rail LEFT of inductor 2: V-AC 0 top (up x~51 to y~136) + inductor 2 left lead (x~115). n2 = bottom rail LEFT of capacitor 11: I-DC 3 bottom (down x~45 to y~384) + capacitor 11 left plate (x~99). n3 = top rail MIDDLE segment: inductor 2 right lead (x~138), zener 4 top (T at (182,141)), diode 5 top (T at (265,141)), capacitor 14 left plate (x~298). n4 = top rail RIGHT segment: capacitor 14 right plate (x~302), zener 10 top (T at (373,142)), diode 8 top (rail corners down at (457,144)). n5 = middle rail RIGHT of capacitor 9: capacitor 9 right plate (x~227), diode 5 bottom + zener 17 top (junction at (262,256)), zener 10 bottom + diode 12 top (junction CIRCLE at (371,258)), diode 8 bottom + diode 6 top (4-way junction at (457,260), verified at 16x), and the rail's right end which runs on to (479,262) and turns down into resistor 13's top lead. n6 = bottom rail MIDDLE segment: capacitor 11 right plate (x~105), diode 16 bottom (junction CIRCLE at (187,382)), zener 17 bottom (junction blob at (257,382)), inductor 1 left lead (x~295). n7 = bottom rail RIGHT segment: inductor 1 right lead (x~323), diode 12 bottom (junction at (364,384)), diode 6 bottom (rail corner at (445,385)). Judgment calls: (a) Every rail/column intersection in this drawing is an explicit junction - the drafter drew either a small open circle ((182,255), (371,258), (187,382)) or a heavy filled blob ((49,256), (262,256), (457,260), (257,382), (364,384)). There is no plain X crossing and no hop anywhere in this schematic, so no crossing judgement was needed; every column is a true 3- or 4-way tie. (b) The three series elements that split the rails were each confirmed at 8-12x to sit IN the rail with the rail wire terminating on each lead: inductor 2 in the top rail, capacitor 9 in the middle rail, capacitor 11 and inductor 1 in the bottom rail, capacitor 14 in the top rail. Capacitor 9 is NOT shorted: only its left plate is on the GND-15 rail; its right plate is on n5, which reaches ground only through resistor 13. (c) 2-terminal terminal order is as drawn: index 0 = top (or left), index 1 = bottom (or right). This does not affect any metric. Device polarities as drawn, for the record: zeners 4 and 10 have the Z-bar at the bottom (cathode down); zener 17 has the Z-bar at the top (cathode up); diodes 5, 8, 12, 16 point downward (cathode down); diode 6 points downward as well; V-AC 0 is unmarked; I-DC 3's arrow points up, i.e. current is driven from the bottom rail into the middle rail. (d) Tier-2 simcheck finding is a real property of the drawing, not a trace error: net n2 touches only I-DC 3's bottom terminal and capacitor 11's left plate, both open at DC, so n2 has no DC path to ground. The ink is unambiguous - I-DC 3 runs down x~45 to y~384 and straight into the left plate of the 5uF capacitor, with nothing else on that segment. A DC current source in series with a capacitor is the standard AC-only textbook construction and is what the drafter drew.
